deep.reconstruction:
The page is almost entirely a drawing. It belongs to the 1981+ dossier on 'systèmes de pseudo-droites', meaning arrangements of pseudo-lines in the (projective or affine) plane.

Main figure:
- A long, nearly horizontal line labelled D0 runs across. At its right end there is a second, overwritten label, probably D5 or D0'.
- Four further lines are labelled D1, D4, D2, D3. Together with D0 they bound a convex pentagonal cell, read cyclically as D0 (top), D4 (right), D3 (lower right), D2 (lower left), D1 (upper left).
- Each label sits on the corresponding side of that cell. The extensions of the lines form star-like (pentagram-type) triangles.
- Two triangular regions below the cell, outside the sides D2 and D3, are hatched. So are a triangle at the top apex between D1 and D4, and some wedges.
- Hatching on one side of a line is the standard way of marking a chosen half-plane (a side, or orientation) of a pseudo-line. The hatched regions are therefore intersections of chosen sides, i.e. cells of the arrangement singled out by sign vectors.
- In the lower half there is a fan of thin, roughly parallel lines running down to the left. This looks like a sweep, a pencil, or a family of further pseudo-lines crossing the configuration.
- A long curved stroke on the right bends sharply and then continues downward. This is plausibly a genuinely non-straight pseudo-line, showing that the objects are topological rather than straight lines.

Marginal sketches on the right show local pictures:
- two pseudo-lines crossing, with a hatched side on each;
- a single 'roof' of two half-lines meeting at an angle, with hatching;
- three lines crossing in a small triangle.

These are the local types of sectors or angles cut out by chosen half-planes at a crossing, and the local picture of a triangular cell.

Context: the previous page has two-sided labels (P/P', Q/Q', L/L', A/A', N/N', ...), suggesting antipodal identification in the projective plane. It also has parameters a, a', b, b' with inequalities a+a' ≤ 2, b+b' ≥ 2 and a'+b > 2, hence b > a. So Grothendieck seems to be studying how cells and sides of a pseudo-line arrangement are combinatorially constrained, plausibly the existence and position of a polygonal cell bounded by several lines, and which adjacent triangles can occur. Questions of this kind lead to triangle flips (mutations), extension of arrangements, and stretchability.

Without the surrounding text, no definite statement can be attached to this page. It is an exploratory figure about cells and half-plane sign data in a small arrangement of 5–6 pseudo-lines.
errors: No claims are written on the page, so there is nothing to check. The drawing itself is schematic; some lines are not drawn straight and some intersections are imprecise, consistent with pseudo-lines.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a bare exploratory figure of a small pseudo-line arrangement with hatched half-planes. It is an interesting witness of Grothendieck's little-known 1980s work on pseudo-lines, but the page itself contains no statement, result or construction beyond standard arrangement pictures.
transcription_corrections: The label 'D_5 [?]' at the right end of the horizontal line is overwritten. It may read D5 or D0' and is ambiguous; it sits on the extension of D0.
The label read as 'D_2' is written in a way that looks like 'Du'/'D_2'; D2 is intended. It labels the lower-left side of the pentagonal cell, and D3 the lower-right side.

Undescribed elements: hatched triangular regions below sides D2 and D3 and at the top apex; a fan of thin parallel lines in the lower part; a long curved pseudo-line on the right; and four marginal sketches of crossings and angles with hatched sides.
